title: Stage 3 — The API
goal: Build a REST API with in-memory storage and connect your Stage 2 UI to it.
summary: HTTP, Express, JSON — the middle layer. Data lives in memory until Stage 4 gives it a real database.

pages.title: Wire the UI to the API

checkpoint.prompt: Fetch the list of workouts without changing anything. Which method?
checkpoint.explanation: GET reads. POST creates. DELETE removes.

checkpoint.prompt: POST successfully creates a workout. Best status code?
checkpoint.explanation: 201 signals a new resource was created.

checkpoint.prompt: You restart the API server. In-memory workouts disappear. Why?

choices.text: RAM is cleared — nothing was written to disk
Express deletes arrays on shutdown intentionally

checkpoint.explanation: In-memory storage is fine for learning; Stage 4 adds real persistence.

checkpoint.prompt: After `const res = await fetch(url)`, how do you get JSON?
Frontend :3000, API :3001 — browser blocks fetch. Likely fix?

choices.text: Enable CORS on the API for the frontend origin
Merge both into one port by deleting the API

checkpoint.explanation: Different ports = different origins. The API must allow the frontend.

checklist.label: `api/` Express app runs on a port
GET returns in-memory records as JSON
POST adds to in-memory store, returns 201
Frontend uses fetch instead of local mock array
Endpoints tested with curl or browser Network tab

questions.prompt: What does the API layer do?

choices.text: Enforces rules and exposes data over HTTP

questions.explanation: The API sits between UI and storage — the contract the frontend calls.

choices.text: Structured text both JavaScript and servers understand
It is the database file format

questions.explanation: JSON is the standard wire format for REST APIs.
Without it, POST bodies are undefined.

questions.prompt: Why use in-memory storage before a real database?

choices.text: Learn HTTP and Express without SQL complexity at the same time

questions.explanation: One layer at a time: UI (2) → API (3) → DB (4).

questions.prompt: Connecting UI to API means replacing…

choices.text: Direct array mutations with fetch() calls

questions.explanation: Keep render logic; change where data is loaded and saved.
